## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

T662 (one fascicle, alt. title 百福莊嚴相經; Sanskrit *Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā-sūtra*) is [地婆訶羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%B0%E5%A9%86%E8%A8%B6%E7%BE%85)'s second rendering of the same Indic *Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā* underlying [T661](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0299). The frontmatter notation 再譯 ("re-translated") indicates that this is a deliberate second attempt by the same translator, presumably reflecting his maturing command of Chinese or a different exemplar of the Indic text.

**Abstract**

T662 is unanimously ascribed to [地婆訶羅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%B0%E5%A9%86%E8%A8%B6%E7%BE%85) (Divākara, 613–687) in the canonical bibliographies. Date bracket follows his attested productive period (676–687). The text is closely parallel to [T661](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0299) but with finer distinctions in the treatment of the "hundred marks of merit" doctrine; the alternate title (*zhuāngyánxiàng* "marks adorning [the body]") emphasizes the role of meritorious roots in actively *adorning* the buddha-body, rather than simply being its causal source. The two versions may derive from slightly different recensions of the *Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā* — though it is more probable that Divākara revised his earlier rendering after acquiring better access to the underlying Sanskrit through later contact with Indian visitors.
